title: Expose agent spawn admission
description:
Objective: expose a first-class startup-admission result from the Claude spawner so callers can distinguish a coded preflight refusal from a process that actually started without waiting for that process to exit.

Deliverable: apps/daemon's spawner provides a start API that returns either the exact SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE refusal code/layer or an accepted start carrying a separate child-exit promise; the existing claudeSpawner exit-lifetime adapter remains compatible for current callers. This is the producer prerequisite for task-58fd2c3781254d839ee27867f8f9f4e6's truthful wrapper report.

NOT in scope: changing agent-wrapper reporting/polling, changing the unquotable character set or Windows command-line builder, weakening validate-before-credential-write, or inventing a generic code for uncoded child-process exceptions.

Verification: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`; both legs must execute, the Vitest leg must print a nonzero Test Files/test count, and no `No projects matched`/zero-test output is acceptable.
definitionOfDone: A public spawner start result distinguishes `{ ok: false, code: "SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE", layer: "agent-spawn-invocation" }` from an accepted start; the refusal test asserts both literals and proves its case count is nonzero.

An accepted start resolves after the child emits startup admission, returns a separate exit promise, and does not wait for the child lifetime before becoming observable; a test holds the child open to prove the distinction.
The existing `claudeSpawner` `(SpawnRequest) => Promise<void>` adapter and its current success/timeout/cleanup behavior remain compatible and its pre-existing tests stay green.
The unquotable refusal still occurs before any credential file is written; accepted starts still remove the credential file on exit/error, asserted from filesystem state rather than call counts.
A mutation drill collapsing the refusal into an accepted start turns the named exact code/layer test red, then the production file is restored byte-for-byte and verified by SHA-256.
Fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` completes under the path-attributed baseline rule, with owned-package legs green and a nonzero daemon test count.
taskRails: This is an interface prerequisite, not a second implementation of spawn validation: call the existing agentSpawnInvocation exactly once and preserve its validate-before-write ordering.
Startup admission and process lifetime are distinct promises/facts. Never await child exit to decide whether startup was admitted.
Catch only the landed typed SpawnInvocationRefusal into the coded start result. Unknown/synchronous child-process failures must not be mislabeled or silently absorbed.
Keep the legacy claudeSpawner adapter so this producer lands independently before its wrapper consumer; do not edit agent-wrapper files in this task.
Preserve explicit-path staging and the per-production-file 250/400 line rail; split a focused helper if agent-spawner.ts would reach 400.

implementationPlan.description: ADD THE PUBLIC START-ADMISSION CONTRACT AND THE NARROW PREFLIGHT BOUNDARY in `agent-spawner.ts`. Keep the existing option surface. For each request, call `agentSpawnInvocation` exactly once inside a catch scoped to that call alone and still before `writeFileSync`; convert only `instanceof SpawnInvocationRefusal` into a frozen exact code/layer refusal using the landed constant. Rethrow every other value unchanged. Do not copy the unquotable character rule, inspect Error messages, add a fallback refusal code, or broaden the catch over credential writing/process creation. Document that Node's `spawn` event admits the spawned shell/process boundary (with `shell:true`, not the inner Claude command's readiness) and that the returned `exit` is the existing bounded lifetime/credential-settlement promise, not independent proof that the OS process is gone after a timeout.

- `agent-spawn-contract.ts` (94 lines): `AgentSpawnerOptions`, the two process-error classes and their reason types, `AgentSpawner`, and the new start-admission types. Declarations only; nothing executes.
`agent-spawner.ts` re-exports every symbol it used to own (`export { AgentProcessContainmentError, AgentProcessFailureError }` and the type set), so no importer sees a change — measured: the only importer outside the test file is `agent-wrapper-main.ts`, which takes `claudeSpawner` and `AgentSpawner`. Result: agent-spawner.ts is 362 lines, under the bar with headroom.

THE CONTRACT. `AgentSpawnStartResult` is the closed union `{ok:false; code:SpawnInvocationRefusalCode; layer:typeof SPAWN_INVOCATION_LAYER} | {ok:true; exit:Promise<void>}`, with the callable `AgentSpawnStart` type and an `AgentSpawnStarter` interface carrying the same `activeCount`/`close` ownership the spawner already had. Refusals are built from the landed `SPAWN_INVOCATION_LAYER` constant, never a literal.

THE NARROW BOUNDARY. `agentSpawnInvocation` is called exactly once per request, still before `writeFileSync`, inside a try whose scope is that ONE call. `if (!(error instanceof SpawnInvocationRefusal)) throw error;` — an unknown throw escapes unchanged, no Error message is inspected, no fallback code exists, and the catch covers neither the credential write nor process creation. The test's spoof error carries `code: "SPAWN_ARGUMENT_UNQUOTABLE"` and `layer: "agent-spawn-invocation"` as own properties and is still rejected unchanged, so only the class — not the shape — can enter the coded arm.

DOCUMENTED IN THE CONTRACT, because both are easy to overstate: with `shell: true` Node's `spawn` event admits the SHELL that was created, not the readiness of the `claude` command inside it; and `exit` is the bounded lifetime/credential-settlement promise this spawner already owned, not independent proof the OS process is gone after a timeout.

implementationPlan.description: IMPLEMENT THE TWO-STAGE CHILD LIFECYCLE AND LEGACY ADAPTER in `agent-spawner.ts`. After successful preflight, write the credential config, invoke the injected spawn, and on a synchronous spawn throw remove that just-written file then reject with the original error. Create distinct start-admission and idempotent lifetime settlement state. Attach `spawn`, `error`, and `exit` listeners immediately after process creation and before writing stdin or arming the timeout: `spawn` alone resolves the accepted start with its still-separate `exit` promise; `error` before admission rejects start unchanged and cleans up; `error` after admission and `exit` settle lifetime/cleanup without retroactively changing admission. Any terminal/timeout path reached while admission is pending must reject uncoded rather than hang or manufacture a stable code. Preserve one-shot timer clearing, credential removal, logging, platform-specific tree kill, and timeout slot release; execute kill cleanup through `try/finally` so a throwing kill cannot strand the promise or credential. Refactor `claudeSpawner` into a compatibility adapter over one `claudeSpawnStarter`: a typed refusal is reconstructed as `SpawnInvocationRefusal` to preserve its existing rejected `Promise<void>` behavior, while an accepted start awaits its `exit` settlement exactly as current callers expect. Keep the production file below 250 physical lines and run the focused test file green with a nonzero test count.
implementationPlan.note:
Two-stage lifecycle and the legacy adapter are in, focused suite at 22 passed / 25 with only the three pre-existing host-dependent reds left.

ADMISSION STATE is separate from lifetime state and can only be RESOLVED by the child's own `spawn` event: `child.on("spawn", admit)`. Denial has three sources, in this order of precedence because a promise keeps its first settlement — the synchronous spawn throw (`denyStart(error)` right after the credential is removed, before `reject(error)`), the child's `error` event (`denyStart(error)` FIRST, so a never-admitted start rejects with the error the runtime actually raised rather than a summary of it), and a catch-all in `cleanup()` that denies with an uncoded `AGENT_SPAWN_NOT_ADMITTED`. That catch-all is what makes a timeout, containment failure, or clean exit reached before admission reject rather than hang, and because deny-after-resolve is a no-op it can never rewrite an admission that already happened.

LISTENER ORDER FIXED to match the step: `close`, `spawn` and `error` are now attached immediately after process creation and BEFORE the timeout is armed and before stdin is written. They were after the timer in the landed code; a child that spawns and dies inside one tick must not be able to outrun its own listeners.

ADAPTER. `spawnRuntime` builds one runtime and hands back both callables over the SAME config directory, active set, containment list and `close`. `claudeSpawner` reconstructs a `SpawnInvocationRefusal` from the coded arm so its existing rejected `Promise<void>` behavior is unchanged, and otherwise awaits `exit` exactly as today — it deliberately does NOT await admission, because the legacy contract is process lifetime and a child that exits without ever emitting `spawn` must still settle the way every current caller has always observed. Its `admitted` promise gets a no-op catch so an unobserved denial cannot surface as an unhandled rejection; the starter does the same for `done` when a start is denied.

Preserved unchanged: one-shot `settled` guarding, timer and kill-timer clearing, credential removal on every settlement path, the wrapper log lines, POSIX negative-pid group kill, Windows taskkill with its confirmation and grace timer, containment failure aggregation, and the timeout slot release. `cleanup()` already wraps the kill-helper teardown in try/catch per call, so a throwing kill cannot strand either the promise or the credential.

It is now 362 — under the hard 400 bar and 37 lines smaller than what I inherited, with the reduction coming from the two focused splits rather than from deleting anything. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Selected a sibling-module `claudeSpawnStarter` plus `AgentSpawnStartResult`, with `claudeSpawner` retained as an adapter. Rejected changing `claudeSpawner` itself to resolve on start because current wrapper callers depend on its process-lifetime/timeout promise. Rejected treating the synchronous return from `spawn()` or a pid as admission, and rejected awaiting child exit before admitting; Node exposes the dedicated `spawn` event for this boundary. Rejected a broad catch/generic spawn code because only `SpawnInvocationRefusal` owns a stable code. Rejected daemon-root publication and a new helper file: the existing `.js` bridge already wildcard-exports the module, the downstream consumer is a sibling daemon module, and root index files are unrelated/shared-tree hotspots.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Fresh measurement at HEAD 2e34a5fe5e65cb936dbfdaf731090ab245382ffd found both owned paths clean. `agent-spawner.ts` is 133 physical lines and calls `agentSpawnInvocation` once at lines 71-75 before `writeFileSync` at 78; its current lifetime promise resolves on exit, error, or timeout. `agent-spawner.test.ts` is 239 lines and already captures the private mkdtemp directory by temporarily redirecting TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP with an exact-one-directory positive control. `agent-spawn-invocation.ts` already exports `SpawnInvocationRefusal`, `SpawnInvocationRefusalCode`, and `SPAWN_INVOCATION_LAYER = "agent-spawn-invocation"`; no validation reimplementation is needed. Official Node child-process semantics state that successful `spawn` precedes other child events, failed spawning emits `error` instead, and `exit` may or may not follow `error`, requiring guarded one-shot settlement. `agent-wrapper.ts:69,226-230` currently consumes `(SpawnRequest)=>Promise<void>` and deletes active work when it settles; this task deliberately leaves it unchanged. The named real consumer is follow-on task `task-912567934d54419683d1518d60059409`. `apps/daemon/package.json` names the workspace package `@moe/daemon` and defines real typecheck/Vitest scripts; `pnpm-workspace.yaml` includes `apps/*`, so the final filter is resolved by package name. This shell lacks pnpm and runs Node 18, while the repo pins Node >=24.16; the worker must run gates in the project-supported environment and verify count output rather than relying on exit code alone.
planningNotes.risks: The event boundary is subtle: with `shell:true`, Node's `spawn` event proves the shell process started, not that the nested Claude command is ready. Attach all listeners before stdin and timeout work so back-to-back events cannot be missed, and guard error/exit because Node permits both. A pre-admission unknown failure must reject unchanged; a post-admission failure must settle lifetime without rewriting the already-observed admission. The timeout promise historically frees the wrapper slot even if kill is only best effort, so document `exit` as bounded lifetime/credential settlement rather than physical-death evidence. The legacy adapter must compose the starter rather than run preflight again. Shared-tree foreign edits exist elsewhere in apps/daemon; do not touch wrapper/root/index files.
